candidate.answerReason: The rays OA and OC can lie on the same side or opposite sides of OB. These possibilities give 70°−30°=40° and 70°+30°=100°, respectively, exhausting the possible angle measures.

methods.label: Consider both ray positions
methods.explanation: Ray \(OC\) may lie outside \(\angle AOB\), giving \(\angle AOC=70^\circ+30^\circ=100^\circ\), or inside \(\angle AOB\), giving \(\angle AOC=70^\circ-30^\circ=40^\circ\). Both cases are possible.
methods.levelReason: Considering the two planar ray positions and using angle addition or subtraction is within Grade 7.

review.mathematicalCheck: For a fixed ray OB, OC has two planar positions making a 30-degree angle with it. Because \(30^\circ<70^\circ\), one lies inside angle AOB and gives \(70^\circ-30^\circ=40^\circ\); the other lies outside and gives \(70^\circ+30^\circ=100^\circ\). These exhaust the possible measures, and the retained explanation covers both.
